job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today, let's discuss Indian rivers. Rohan, why do Himalayan rivers flow all year? Rohan: I think it is because of the heavy rainfall in the mountains. Teacher: Actually, that is a common error. They are perennial because they receive water from both melting snow and seasonal rain. Priya, what about the Narmada and Tapi? Priya: They flow south like the Ganga, right? Teacher: Not quite. Unlike most rivers flowing into the Bay of Bengal, these two flow westwards into the Arabian Sea. Now, consider a drainage basin. It is not just the river channel; it includes the entire area drained by a single river system, including all its tributaries. Finally, regarding pollution, we must realize it is not just industrial waste. Urban sewage, agricultural runoff, and religious offerings also significantly degrade our water quality. We must look at the entire system to understand these rivers properly.

items.evidence: They are perennial because they receive water from both melting snow and seasonal rain.
items.q: Why do Himalayan rivers keep flowing even in the dry months?
options: Snowmelt adds water when the rains stop
Heavy mountain rain falls through the whole year
They begin in plains and flow uphill
They are older and bigger than other rivers
items.explain: Himalayan rivers get water from melting snow as well as seasonal rain, so they flow all year.

wrong.why: thinks rainfall alone keeps them flowing
thinks the rivers start in plains and flow upward
thinks age and size explain constant flow

items.evidence: Unlike most rivers flowing into the Bay of Bengal, these two flow westwards into the Arabian Sea.
items.q: A boat is dropped into the Narmada river. Which sea will it finally reach?
options: The Arabian Sea, in the west
The Bay of Bengal, in the east
The Arabian Sea, after turning south
The Bay of Bengal, like the Ganga
items.explain: The Narmada and Tapi flow westwards and drain into the Arabian Sea, unlike most Peninsular rivers.

wrong.why: thinks Narmada flows east like most Peninsular rivers
thinks all rivers flow north to south
copies the Ganga's route onto the Narmada

items.evidence: It is not just the river channel; it includes the entire area drained by a single river system, including all its tributaries.
items.q: Rain falls on a hill far from the Ganga's channel. When is it part of its basin?
options: When its water drains into the Ganga system
When the hill lies right beside the channel
When the rain falls directly into the channel
When the hill is higher than the channel
items.explain: A drainage basin is the whole area drained by a river system and its tributaries, not only the channel.

wrong.why: thinks the basin is only the channel and its edge
thinks only water falling in the channel counts

items.evidence: Urban sewage, agricultural runoff, and religious offerings also significantly degrade our water quality.
items.q: A factory near a river is closed down. Will the river become fully clean?
options: No, sewage and farm runoff still pollute it
Yes, factories are the only source of pollution
Yes, because rivers clean themselves quickly
No, because religious offerings are the only cause
items.explain: Pollution also comes from urban sewage, agricultural runoff and religious offerings, not just industrial waste.

wrong.why: thinks pollution is only industrial waste
over-generalises one named source as the only cause
